draft.title: The cerebral cortex and its lobes
card: The cerebral cortex is the thin, folded outer layer of the forebrain. Each half of it is split into four lobes, and each lobe has main jobs.
planning, decision making, voluntary movement and speech production. It sits at the front of the brain.
processes touch and body position. It sits behind the frontal lobe, near the top of the head.
The temporal lobe, near the ears, handles hearing and memory. The occipital lobe, at the back of the brain, handles vision.
draft.remember: Frontal: plan, move, speak. Parietal: touch. Temporal: hear, remember. Occipital: see.

a.q: Jo is learning to hold a pen. Which lobe mainly processes the feeling of the pen against her fingers?
a.why: The parietal lobe processes touch and body position, so it deals with the feel of the pen. The frontal lobe is the tempting choice because it controls voluntary movement, but it directs the movement and does not process the touch.

b.q: After a stroke, Sam can see and hear normally and feels objects in his hand. He now struggles to plan his day and to form words when he speaks. Which lobe was most likely damaged?
b.why: Planning and speech production are jobs of the frontal lobe. The temporal lobe is tempting because it handles hearing, but Sam hears normally, and his trouble is in producing speech, not in hearing it.
b.clue: Sam's senses work. Which lobe handles planning and speech production?
